mainTopic: ברכת חתנים: days for a widow, the source for ten men, ברכת אירוסין, and the seven days of celebration
overview: The גמרא first brings a ברייתא that seems to give every widow only one day of ברכת חתנים. It answers that the ברייתא means a widow who marries an אלמן, and that the ברייתא only listed minimums that always hold. Next, רב נחמן learns that ברכת חתנים needs ten men from the ten elders of בועז. רבי אבהו learns it instead from 'בְּמַקְהֵלוֹת' in תהלים. Each side then explains what he does with the other's פסוק. Along the way, the גמרא rules that giving ownership to an unborn baby does not work. Then ברייתות teach where ברכת חתנים and ברכת אירוסין are said, and the גמרא gives the text of ברכת אירוסין, with a debate about its closing line. Finally, it teaches that ברכת חתנים is said with ten men all seven days when פנים חדשות come. It then begins listing the wedding blessings, a list that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to give every widow only one day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the earlier view that a widow who marries a בחור gets seven days. It quotes a ברייתא that gives a widow only one day, and suggests this means every widow.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: We say the blessing for a virgin for seven days, and for a widow for one day. Doesn't this mean even a widow who marries a bachelor?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to attack the earlier idea that a widow who marries a בחור gets seven days of ברכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא splits brides into only two groups: בתולה gets seven days, and אלמנה gets one day. It does not mention who the groom is. So it sounds like every widow gets only one day, even one who marries a בחור, and that goes against the earlier statement.

keyTerms.meaning: We say the blessing (here, ברכת חתנים)
A virgin bride, marrying for the first time
A bachelor, a man marrying for the first time
Doesn't it mean...? (a way of suggesting how to read a source)

phrases.english: They challenged: We say the blessing for a virgin for seven days
phrases.notes: This is aimed at the earlier statement that a widow who marries a בחור gets seven days.

phrases.english: and for a widow for one day.
Doesn't this mean
even a widow who marries a bachelor!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier statement, before this part of the text, that a widow who marries a בחור gets seven days.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a widow marrying a בחור gets seven days of ברכת חתנים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא gives an אלמנה one day without any limit, so it seems to include an אלמנה who marries a בחור.

steps.title: The ברייתא means a widow who marries a widower
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא's one day is only for a widow who marries an אלמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means a widow who marries a widower.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the earlier view. It says the ברייתא's 'one day' is talking only about a widow who marries a widower.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By narrowing the ברייתא to a widow who marries an אלמן, the conflict goes away. A widow who marries a בחור is simply not the case the ברייתא is talking about, so she can still get seven days.

keyTerms.meaning: A widower, a man whose wife died

phrases.english: No, it means a widow married to a widower.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 by limiting the ברייתא to a narrower case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the ברייתא is about a widow who marries an אלמן.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's one day applies to every widow.
steps.terutzMaskana: The one day applies only to a widow who marries an אלמן; a widow who marries a בחור can still get seven days.

steps.title: Then why didn't the ברייתא list the middle case?
steps.stepSummary: If a widow who marries a בחור gets seven days, the ברייתא should have listed three cases, not two.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for a bachelor, what? Seven days? If so, let it teach: We say the blessing for a virgin seven days, for a widow who marries a bachelor seven days, and for a widow one day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. If the widow who marries a בחור really gets seven days, why didn't the ברייתא say so clearly?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא could easily have listed three cases: בתולה, אלמנה with a בחור, and אלמנה with an אלמן. Leaving out the middle case looks strange if it has its own different rule. This suggests the ברייתא really meant every widow gets one day.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, if that is true
Let it teach, it should have said

phrases.english: But for a widow married to a bachelor, what? Seven days?
If so, let it teach:
We say the blessing for a virgin for seven days,
and for a widow who marries a bachelor seven days,
and for a widow one day?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל לְבָחוּר מַאי, שִׁבְעָה? אִי הָכִי לִיתְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 2 by pointing to how the ברייתא is worded.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא is talking only about a widow who marries an אלמן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a widow marrying a בחור had a different rule (seven days), the ברייתא should have listed her as a separate third case.

steps.title: The ברייתא only teaches rules that always hold
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists only fixed minimums: a בתולה never gets less than seven days, and an אלמנה never gets less than one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches a fixed, clear-cut rule: there is no virgin who gets less than seven days, and there is no widow who gets less than one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא left out the middle case. It only wanted to state rules with no exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every בתולה gets seven days, with no exceptions. Every אלמנה gets at least one day, but some (those who marry a בחור) get more. The ברייתא gave each group's guaranteed minimum and did not go into details, so the earlier view still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A clear-cut rule with no exceptions

steps.whatToRemember: An אלמנה who marries an אלמן gets one day of ברכת חתנים. An אלמנה who marries a בחור can get seven. The ברייתא only gave the minimum that always applies to each group.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא's 'one day for a widow' is a minimum, not a fixed amount for every widow. Some widows get more.

phrases.english: It teaches a clear-cut matter,
for there is no virgin who gets less than seven days,
and there is no widow who gets less than one day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of step 3 and closes this back-and-forth.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the ברייתא's style: it lists only rules that always hold, not every detail.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא left out the widow with a בחור because she has no separate rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: She was left out because her rule is not true of all widows; the ברייתא gave only guaranteed minimums.

steps.title: רב נחמן: ten men for ברכת חתנים, from the ten elders of בועז
steps.stepSummary: Going back to an earlier statement, רב נחמן quotes a ברייתא that ברכת חתנים needs ten men, learned from בועז gathering ten elders.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the main topic. רב נחמן said: הונא בר נתן told me that a ברייתא taught: Where do we learn that ברכת חתנים needs ten men? As it says: 'He took ten men of the elders of the city and said: Sit here.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now returns to a statement it mentioned earlier and looks at it in full: the source that ברכת חתנים needs a מנין of ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When בועז married רות, he gathered exactly ten elders. From this, the ברייתא learns that ברכת חתנים needs ten men present. This step opens a new topic, about the source for the ten, separate from the question of how many days.

keyTerms.meaning: Back to the statement itself, now discussed in full

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source used for the practical rule that שבע ברכות need a מנין of ten.

phrases.english: Back to the statement itself. רב נחמן said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לִי הוּנָא בַּר נָתָן, תָּנָא:
phrases.english: הונא בר נתן told me that a ברייתא taught:
From where do we learn that ברכת חתנים is said with ten?
As it says: 'He took ten men'
'of the elders of the city and said: Sit here.'
phrases.notes: רות 4:2. The 'he' here is בועז, getting ready to marry רות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of how many days and goes back to a statement quoted earlier, to discuss it in full.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ברכת חתנים needs ten men, learned from the ten elders בועז gathered.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: the source is a פסוק in תהלים
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו brings a different source for the ten: 'In assemblies bless God... from the source of ישראל.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אבהו said, the source is from here: 'In assemblies bless God, the Lord, from the source of ישראל.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives a second, different פסוק to show that ברכת חתנים needs ten men.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Assemblies' (מקהלות) means a group, a קהל of at least ten. 'The source of ישראל' is read as having to do with where Jewish children come from, meaning marriage. So the blessing over marriage is said in a group of ten.

keyTerms.meaning: In assemblies, in gatherings of people

phrases.english: And רבי אבהו said: from here:
'In assemblies bless God,'
'the Lord, from the source of ישראל.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different פסוק for the same rule that רב נחמן taught in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The need for ten men at ברכת חתנים comes from 'בְּמַקְהֵלוֹת... מִמְּקוֹר יִשְׂרָאֵל'.

steps.title: What does רב נחמן learn from רבי אבהו's פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב נחמן does with the פסוק from תהלים, since he does not use it for ten men.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן, what does he learn from this פסוק of רבי אבהו?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It asks how רב נחמן reads the פסוק that רבי אבהו used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes every פסוק teaches something. If רב נחמן doesn't use this פסוק for the ten men, he must use it for something else. The גמרא wants to know what that is.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב נַחְמָן, בְּהַאי קְרָא דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
phrases.english: And רב נחמן, from this פסוק of רבי אבהו,
what does he learn from it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב נַחְמָן, בְּהַאי קְרָא דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ מַאי דָּרֵישׁ בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the two sources by asking how רב נחמן reads רבי אבהו's פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson רב נחמן takes from 'בְּמַקְהֵלוֹת בָּרְכוּ אֱלֹהִים... מִמְּקוֹר יִשְׂרָאֵל'.

steps.title: רב נחמן uses the פסוק for babies singing at the sea
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן needs the פסוק for רבי מאיר's teaching that even unborn babies sang שירה at the sea.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what a ברייתא teaches: רבי מאיר used to say: Where do we learn that even unborn babies in their mothers' wombs sang שירה at the sea? As it says: 'In assemblies bless God, the Lord, from the source of ישראל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב נחמן uses the פסוק for something else: to teach that even babies still in the womb sang at קריעת ים סוף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי מאיר's reading, 'מקור' means the womb. So the פסוק says that even those still 'in the source' (unborn babies) joined the assemblies praising God. Since the פסוק is already used for this, רב נחמן does not use it for ten men.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different lesson)
The song at the sea (אז ישיר)

phrases.english: He needs it for what a ברייתא teaches:
רבי מאיר used to say:
From where do we learn that even babies in their mothers' wombs
sang the song at the sea?
As it says: 'In assemblies bless God,'
'the Lord, from the source of ישראל.'
phrases.notes: Here 'source' is read as the womb, so even those still inside joined the praise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב נחמן uses the פסוק for רבי מאיר's teaching that even unborn babies sang שירה at the sea.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: 'מקור' means matters of the source, not the womb
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו answers that if the פסוק meant the womb, it would have said 'מבטן'. The word 'מקור' points to matters of the source, meaning marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (רבי אבהו)? If so, let the פסוק say 'from the belly.' Why does it say 'from the source'? It means matters having to do with the source.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי אבהו deals with רבי מאיר's reading, and answers that the exact word 'מקור' proves his own reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק only wanted to say unborn babies sang, the clearer word would be 'מבטן' (from the belly). Choosing 'מקור' hints at 'matters of the source', meaning marriage and having children. So רבי אבהו learns from it that ברכת חתנים is said in a group of ten.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one? (How does the other opinion answer?)
Matters of the source, meaning marriage and having children

steps.whatToRemember: Both רב נחמן (from בועז's ten elders) and רבי אבהו (from 'בְּמַקְהֵלוֹת') agree ברכת חתנים needs ten men. They only argue about which פסוק is the source.

phrases.english: And the other one? If so,
phrases.notes: 'The other one' is רבי אבהו, explaining why he doesn't read the פסוק like רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: let the פסוק say 'from the belly.'
What does 'from the source' mean?
It is about matters of the source.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי אבהו's side: why he does not accept the reading of the פסוק given in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'מקור' instead of 'בטן' shows the פסוק is about matters of the source, meaning marriage, so it teaches the ten for ברכת חתנים.

steps.title: What does רבי אבהו learn from בועז's ten elders?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי אבהו does with רב נחמן's verse about בועז.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אבהו, what does he learn from the verse that רב נחמן used?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the question around. It already asked what רב נחמן does with רבי אבהו's verse, and now it asks what רבי אבהו does with רב נחמן's verse about בועז.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side has a verse the other side doesn't use for ten men. The גמרא assumes no verse is extra, so רבי אבהו must use בועז's ten elders for something else. The next step tells us what.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he learn from it?

phrases.english: And רבי אבהו,
this verse used by רב נחמן,
what does he learn from it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ, בְּהַאי קְרָא דְּרַב נַחְמָן מַאי דָּרֵישׁ בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors the question of Step 7, now aimed at רבי אבהו
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי אבהו learns from the verse of בועז's ten elders

steps.title: The elders were there to rule about Moabite women
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו uses the verse for the ruling 'an Ammonite man, not an Ammonite woman; a Moabite man, not a Moabite woman.' Using elders shows it was a ruling, not a blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs that verse to teach: an Ammonite man is forbidden, not an Ammonite woman; a Moabite man, not a Moabite woman. If the gathering were only for a blessing, ordinary men would have been enough without elders.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for רבי אבהו, בועז gathered the elders to publicly rule that the ban on marrying a Moabite applies only to men. That would allow רות to marry into ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is the word 'elders.' A blessing does not need elders, but a legal ruling does need wise judges. So the gathering was a court session, not a ברכת חתנים.

keyTerms.meaning: An Ammonite man, not an Ammonite woman
A Moabite man, not a Moabite woman

phrases.english: He needs that verse in order to teach:
an Ammonite man, and not an Ammonite woman,
phrases.notes: The Torah's ban on marrying into these nations is in דברים 23:4.

phrases.english: a Moabite man, and not a Moabite woman.
For if you would think it was for the blessing,
wouldn't men who are not elders have been enough?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse teaches that only Ammonite and Moabite men are forbidden, and the elders show it was a legal ruling, not a blessing

steps.title: רב נחמן asks why a ruling would need ten
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן pushes back: if it was only to teach a law, why gather exactly ten?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (רב נחמן) says: if you think it was to teach a law, wouldn't fewer than ten have been enough?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן attacks רבי אבהו's reading. Teaching a law does not need ten people, so why did בועז gather exactly ten?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side points to a detail in the verse. רבי אבהו points to 'elders,' which fits a ruling. רב נחמן points to 'ten,' which fits a ברכה with a מנין.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one, meaning the other side of the debate

phrases.english: And the other one:
phrases.notes: This is רב נחמן answering back to רבי אבהו.

phrases.english: If you would think it was in order to teach a law,
wouldn't fewer than ten have been enough!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ: אִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ לְמִידְרַשׁ, לָא סַגִּיא דְּלָאו עֲשָׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof given in Step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's claim that the gathering was for teaching a law
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Teaching a law does not need ten, so the number ten suggests a ברכה that needs a quorum

steps.title: Ten were gathered to make the ruling public
steps.stepSummary: Ten is not required for a ruling, but בועז gathered ten to publicize it, just as שמואל did.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, ten is not required, but it was done to publicize the matter. Like שמואל said to רב חנא of Baghdad: go bring me ten men, and I will tell you in front of them: one who gives ownership to an unborn baby, the baby acquires it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees that teaching a law does not need ten. It explains that בועז gathered ten so the ruling would become widely known. It brings a case where שמואל did the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer saves רבי אבהו. The elders show the gathering was for a ruling, and the number ten was for making it public. שמואל's story shows that sages did gather ten to spread a ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: One who gives ownership to an unborn baby

phrases.english: Yes, but it was to publicize the matter,
just as שמואל said
to רב חנא of Baghdad:
Go and bring me a group of ten,
and I will tell you in front of them:
One who gives ownership to an unborn baby, it acquires.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concedes the point and gives a different reason for the ten
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Gathering ten must mean a ברכה that needs a quorum
steps.terutzMaskana: Ten can also be gathered just to make a ruling public, as שמואל did

steps.title: The הלכה: an unborn baby does not acquire
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules against שמואל's statement: giving ownership to an unborn baby does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: one who gives ownership to an unborn baby, it does not acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: Since שמואל's ruling was just mentioned, the גמרא stops to give the final הלכה on it. The הלכה goes against שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a side note, not part of the ten-men debate. שמואל's story was brought only to show that people gathered ten to publicize a ruling. The actual law on unborn babies is different.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא accepts שמואל's ruling just because it used his story. The story only proves that ten were gathered to publicize something. The הלכה goes the other way.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: one who gives ownership to an unborn baby, it does not acquire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Side ruling on the case quoted in Step 13
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Giving ownership to an unborn baby does not take effect

steps.title: Where is ברכת חתנים said?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says ברכת חתנים is said at the wedding house. רבי יהודה says it may be said at the אירוסין too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: ברכת חתנים is said in the house of the grooms. רבי יהודה says: it is said even in the house of the betrothal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא about where ברכת חתנים is said. The תנא קמא says the wedding house, and רבי יהודה adds the house of the אירוסין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual time for this blessing is the wedding (נישואין). רבי יהודה allows it even earlier, at the betrothal. The next step explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: The house of the grooms, where the wedding takes place

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
We say the grooms' blessing in the house of the grooms.
רבי יהודה says:
We say it even in the house of the betrothal.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מְבָרְכִין בִּרְכַּת חֲתָנִים בְּבֵית חֲתָנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about where ברכת חתנים is said
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ברכת חתנים is said at the wedding house; רבי יהודה says even at the אירוסין

steps.title: אביי explains: in יהודה the couple was alone together
steps.stepSummary: אביי says רבי יהודה's rule was taught for יהודה, where the groom was secluded with his betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: they taught this in יהודה, because there he is secluded with her.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains when רבי יהודה's rule applies. In יהודה, a betrothed couple used to be alone together, so the blessing was said already at the betrothal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's rule is not for every place. It depends on the custom in יהודה, where a couple could be alone together before the wedding. That made it fitting to say the ברכה at the betrothal.
steps.whatToRemember: ברכת חתנים is normally said at the wedding. רבי יהודה allows it at the אירוסין, and אביי says that was because of the custom in יהודה, where the couple was alone together.

phrases.english: אביי said:
They taught this in יהודה,
phrases.notes: He means רבי יהודה's rule about saying the ברכה at the betrothal.

phrases.english: because there he is alone with her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits and explains רבי יהודה's view from Step 15
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה's rule applies in יהודה, where the groom was alone with his betrothed

steps.title: Another teaching: each blessing belongs at its own event
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא says ברכת חתנים is said at the wedding, and ברכת אירוסין is said at the betrothal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: the grooms' blessing is said at the wedding, and the betrothal blessing is said at the betrothal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another ברייתא that gives each of the two blessings its own place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 discussed saying ברכת חתנים even at the אירוסין. This ברייתא clarifies that there are two separate blessings: ברכת חתנים for the wedding (נישואין) and a different blessing, ברכת אירוסין, for the betrothal.

keyTerms.meaning: The wedding blessings said for the groom and bride
The blessing said at the betrothal
The place or event where the betrothal happens

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two blessings. ברכת חתנים is the wedding blessing, and ברכת אירוסין is a separate blessing for the betrothal.

phrases.english: It is taught in another baraita:
One recites the blessing of the grooms
in the house of the grooms,
phrases.notes: He means the wedding itself, the נישואין.

phrases.english: and the blessing of betrothal in the house of the betrothal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second ברייתא on the same subject, separating the wedding blessing from the betrothal blessing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ברכת חתנים is said at the wedding, and ברכת אירוסין is said at the betrothal.

steps.title: What are the words of the betrothal blessing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the exact wording of ברכת אירוסין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The betrothal blessing: what does one say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a plain question to set up the next step: what are the actual words of ברכת אירוסין?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא named ברכת אירוסין but did not give its text. This question opens the discussion of its wording.

phrases.english: The blessing of the betrothal, what does one recite?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the wording of the blessing the ברייתא just mentioned.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact text of ברכת אירוסין.

steps.title: The text of the betrothal blessing
steps.stepSummary: Two sages, quoting רב יהודה, give the text: ה׳ commanded us about the עריות, forbade us betrothed women, and permitted women married through חופה and קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין בר רב אדא and רבה בר רב אדא both said in the name of רב יהודה: Blessed are You, ה׳ our God, King of the world, Who made us holy with His מצוות, commanded us about forbidden relationships, forbade us betrothed women, and permitted us women who are married through חופה and קידושין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by giving the full wording of ברכת אירוסין, quoted from רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blessing thanks ה׳ for the rules of marriage. A betrothed woman is still forbidden to be together with her husband, and she becomes permitted only after the full process of חופה and קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothed women, after קידושין but before the wedding
The wedding canopy and betrothal, the two stages of marriage

phrases.aramaic: רָבִין בַּר רַב אַדָּא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב אַדָּא,
phrases.english: Ravin bar Rav Adda and Rabba bar Rav Adda,
both of them said in the name of Rav Yehuda:
Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe,
Who sanctified us with His מצוות,
and commanded us concerning forbidden relationships,
and forbade to us the betrothed women,
phrases.notes: Even your own betrothed is still off-limits until the wedding.

phrases.english: and permitted to us the married women
by means of the wedding canopy and betrothal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the wording.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The blessing praises ה׳ for forbidding the עריות and betrothed women, and for permitting women married through חופה and קידושין.

steps.title: Adding a closing line to the blessing
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא, also quoting רב יהודה, adds a closing: Blessed are You ה׳, Who sanctifies ישראל through חופה and קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא ends the blessing in the name of רב יהודה: Blessed are You, ה׳, Who makes ישראל holy through חופה and קידושין.
steps.whatsHappening: A different version of רב יהודה's teaching adds a closing line (חתימה) to ברכת אירוסין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The body of the blessing is the same. The only new thing is a second "ברוך אתה ה׳" at the end, which the version in step 19 did not have.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא מְסַיֵּים בַּהּ
phrases.english: Rav Aha, son of Rava, concludes it
in the name of Rav Yehuda:
Blessed are You, Lord, Who sanctifies Israel
by means of the wedding canopy and betrothal.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא מְסַיֵּים בַּהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the same blessing, with a closing line added.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ברכת אירוסין ends with "ברוך אתה ה׳ מקדש ישראל על ידי חופה וקידושין".

steps.title: Why one view has a closing line and one does not
steps.stepSummary: The view without a חתימה compares this blessing to blessings on food and מצוות. The view with a חתימה compares it to קידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who does not add an ending treats it like the blessing on fruit and the blessing on מצוות. The one who adds an ending treats it like קידוש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind each version of the blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blessings on food and on מצוות say "ברוך אתה ה׳" only at the start. קידוש says it both at the start and at the end. Each side compares ברכת אירוסין to a different model of blessing.

keyTerms.meaning: Concludes with a closing "ברוך אתה ה׳"
The blessing on fruit and food
קידוש of שבת and יום טוב

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions share the same text for ברכת אירוסין. They argue only about the closing line: one treats it like a short blessing on food or a מצוה, and the other treats it like קידוש.

phrases.english: The one who does not conclude,

phrases.aramaic: מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַבִּרְכַּת פֵּרוֹת וְאַבִּרְכַּת מִצְוֹת.
phrases.english: it is just like the blessing over fruits and the blessing over מצוות.
phrases.notes: Those blessings say "ברוך אתה ה׳" only once, at the beginning.

phrases.english: And the one who concludes,
it is just like kiddush.
phrases.notes: קידוש says "ברוך אתה ה׳" at both the start and the end.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the two versions in steps 19 and 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The disagreement over the closing line depends on which model of blessing ברכת אירוסין follows.

steps.title: Wedding blessings with ten men for seven days
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that ברכת חתנים is said with a group of ten men during all seven days of the celebration.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: ברכת חתנים is said with ten men all seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic: how long ברכת חתנים continues after the wedding, and with how many people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ברכת חתנים is not said only once at the wedding. It is repeated at the meals during the שבעה days, but only when ten men are present.

keyTerms.meaning: All seven days of the wedding celebration

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One recites the blessing of the grooms with ten men
all seven days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about ברכת חתנים during the seven days.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ברכת חתנים is said with ten men during all seven days of celebration.

steps.title: Only when new guests come
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה limits the rule: the blessings are repeated only when פנים חדשות, new people, have come.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: That is only when new faces have come.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה adds a condition to the ברייתא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ten men alone is not enough on the later days. Someone new, who was not at the earlier celebration, must also be present for the full blessings to be said again.

keyTerms.meaning: New faces, people who were not at the earlier celebration

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source of the practical rule that שבע ברכות during the week need פנים חדשות.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
And that is when new faces came.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: וְהוּא שֶׁבָּאוּ פָּנִים חֲדָשׁוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition to the ברייתא's seven-day rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ברכת חתנים is repeated during the seven days only when new people have come.

steps.title: What are the wedding blessings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the wording of ברכת חתנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does one say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next step by asking what the actual words of ברכת חתנים are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the discussion was about when and where these blessings are said. Now the גמרא turns to their actual text.

phrases.english: What does one recite?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rules for saying ברכת חתנים to its actual text.

steps.title: רב יהודה begins listing the wedding blessings
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה starts giving the text of ברכת חתנים, beginning with the standard opening of a blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: Blessed are You, ה׳ our God, King of the world,
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה begins answering with the text of the blessings. The list continues past this point in the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the opening words appear here. The rest of the blessings are listed in the text that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: King of the world, the standard opening of a blessing

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question about the wording.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב יהודה begins giving the text of ברכת חתנים; the full list continues afterward.
